# `frame` dialect

CEIR-15 sec-39 the ceir.frame dialect: the AUTHORABLE FRAME GRAPH as CEIR (REN-36's .frame.toml asset system, promoted). A frame.graph REGION contains the frame's resource.declare/import ops (graph-owned + external resources -- the frame graph's resources ARE resource dialect values, so the CEIR-12b/c/d lifetime/alias/memory planner plans them; NO parallel frame.resource op), its frame.draw_list ECS-query declares, and its frame.pass work-unit nodes. A pass' MECHANIC is a registered ExecutorTypeId named by the `executor` SYMBOL attr (never one-op-per-executor -- that recreates the retired FramePassKind enum); its read/written resources ride ONE variadic `resources` operand tail tokened by the `access` string (opgen: only the last operand may be variadic -- the 13a compute.dispatch / 14b render.draw house pattern), so CEIR's resource_root + ops_hazard machinery DERIVES the frame's barriers + transient lifetimes (the sec-159 realization: topology/lifetime/history become a CEIR analysis pass, not a hand-rolled one). HISTORY (ping-pong / TAA prev-frame) rides resource.declare's EXISTING lifetime=history + history_length (CEIR-12b); frame.history(R) is the prev-frame READ -- a distinct op whose result is its own resource_root, so a read-of-prev vs write-of-curr does NOT derive a false intra-frame RAW (the RMW scar's frame edition, fixed STRUCTURALLY). Frame-scoped SIZING (width/height/scale/samples/mips/depth_buffer/no_alias/resizable) + buffer usage (indirect_args/structured/counter) ride as OPEN attrs on the resource.declare inside a frame.graph region (the open-attr precedent is IN-dialect: declare already carries open planner tags streaming_priority/budget_class), validated by Context::find_frame_misuse WHEN the declare sits in a frame.graph region. Executor-specific pass config (shader/kernel/technique/draw_list/clear/blend/depth/sampler/render-state/role-bits) rides as OPEN attrs on frame.pass, validated at COOK against the EXECUTOR's schema (15c), NOT the op verifier -- CEIR attrs are an open set (the opgen verifier checks only required attrs). Migration: .frame.toml + FrameGraphBuilder both END at ceir.frame via a FrameGraphDesc<->ceir.frame converter pair with a round-trip-identity gate (15a-3); the old runtime consumes ceir.frame through the backward converter (incremental 15e); ADR-0106 superseded in place @ 15f; asset IDs preserved. ADR-0127. Reference/interpreter semantics = a NAMED-FORWARD typed NoSemantics (the resource/async precedent): a frame op executes when the frame runtime + provider binding land (15d/15e).

**4 ops:** `draw_list`, `graph`, `history`, `pass`

## `frame.pass`

A frame work-unit node: run the `executor` MECHANIC over the `resources` (tokened by `access`), inside a frame.graph.

frame.pass(%resources...) { executor=@mechanic, access="...", for_each, queue, shader?/kernel?/technique?, <open executor params> } -- RESULTLESS, legal ONLY inside a frame.graph region. Effects: GPUCommand + ambient MemoryReadWrite (15d narrows per-operand from access). find_frame_misuse: executor a Symbol (ExecutorNotSymbol); access token-count == num operands + tokens in {r,w,rw}; for_each/queue closed vocabularies; every operand resource- or draw_list-kinded. Executor-specific params ride as OPEN attrs, validated at cook against the executor schema (15c). NestedNonFrameOp if outside a frame.graph region. CEIR-15c-1a per-operand guards: every operand DEFINED in this frame.graph region (OperandOutsideGraph); a lifetime=history resource is READ only via frame.history, never as a direct r/rw operand (HistoryReadNotThroughFrameHistory); a frame.history result is never WRITTEN (HistoryWriteThroughHistory).
